Linear Controls Overview The standard and most widely used method for control Linear controls. However, inpractice, thesystemtobecontrolledisrarelylinear. Therefore, a linear approximation must be used to develop and analyze a control scheme. That is, a reasonable operating point for the system is chosen and the system is linearized about this operating point. The linearized system is a valid representation of the system within some neighborhood of this operating point. However, if there is a sufficiently large swing in any system state, the system may swing into a nonlinear region of operation so that the linear approximation is no longer valid. That is, the stability criteria may no longer apply and the controller may begin to drive the system to an unstable operating point. Direct application of nonlinear controls to nonlinear systems helps to circumvent some of these issues. The nonlinear controls approach utilized in this paper is detailed in the next section. 3.1.
